question.text: Two point charges <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of magnitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> respectively are placed at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> apart. The electric field at the middle point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi></math> between the charges is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The distance '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math>' between the point charges <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Direction of electric field at mid-point due to both charge will be in same direction, which is towards right.

Therefore, E at mid-point =kqd22+kqd22 

⇒6.4×104=2×9×109×8×10-6d2×4

⇒d=3 m
